correctness.rationale: A cyclic word with q^n-1 distinct n-windows gives a closed edge-simple trail in the directed de Bruijn graph. Subtracting its balanced degrees from the full degrees shows that the sole missing edge is a loop, hence a^n. Removing such a loop from a full tour is exactly deletion within its constant run; the run cannot be longer because the loop occurs only once. Deleting outside the q disjoint constant windows preserves every loop and therefore cannot yield a qualifying trail. This gives qn successful indexed positions and q distinct outcomes. In a shortened trail the vertex a^(n-1) has q-1 outgoing incidences. Inserting the missing loop at each restores a full tour. Distinct gaps yield distinct cyclic tours since deleting the unique loop recovers the cyclic order of distinct old edges with the gap identified. Thus double counting gives q D_q(n)/(q-1) with the stated classical D_q(n). Independently, deleting a loop leaves all rooted arborescence counts unchanged and changes just one BEST factorial from (q-1)! to (q-2)!, verifying the fixed-letter count. For n=1 the graph has one vertex and q labeled loops; deletion works at every letter, there are (q-2)! shortened cyclic orders per missing letter, and insertion has q-1 gaps, including the single gap for q=2.
residual_risks: The fresh exhaustive checks are restricted to (q,n)=(2,1),(2,2),(2,3),(2,4),(3,1),(3,2),(4,1). They confirm deletion sets, restoration fibers and both census formulas only in those cases; the graph proof is general.

evidence: Omitting one balanced edge forces a loop; for a specified loop BEST keeps the tree factor and divides the degree-factorial product by q-1. This recovers the full census by summing over q letters, without needing an additional structural lemma.

With the loop restriction known, deletion succeeds exactly within one of the constant windows by the classical puncturing rule and preservation of any constant window not intersecting the edit. Distinct inverse gaps use the unique restored loop and the edge labels, giving q-1.
The neighboring trace-spectrum result is for all distinct deletion-output necklaces, not a prior explicit filter to window-distinct outputs.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Census and edit fragility require only immediate consequences of prior balance, loop counting and puncturing; the combined statement is not an independent addition to that coverage.

evidence: Classical puncturing deletes the distinguished constant n-window's letter; §8.2.4 gives the reverse insertion rule, the q-1 occurrences of the constant (n-1)-block, and the count of full cycles.

At length q^n-1 for n>=2, every (n-1)-word occurs because each has q possible n-word extensions and at most one can be missing. Thus the frozen shortened cycles coincide with the prior generalized de Bruijn classes at that length, with the same rotation convention.
